phrases.evening_greeting: Bonsoir, comment s'est passée votre journée?
phrases.polite_response: Je vais bien, merci de demander

grammar.explanation: In French, use 'Bonjour' for formal situations and 'Salut' for informal ones. 'Vous' is formal 'you', 'tu' is informal.
examples: Comment allez-vous? → Quoi de neuf? (formal → informal)

conversation.speaker: Alex
conversation.text: Bonjour Sarah ! Comment ça va?
conversation.translation: Good morning Sarah! How are you?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.text: Bonjour Alex ! Je vais bien, merci. Et toi?
conversation.translation: Good morning Alex! I'm doing well, thank you. How about you?

conversation.speaker: Alex
conversation.text: Je vais très bien, merci ! Bonne journée!
conversation.translation: I'm great, thanks! Have a good day!

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.text: Toi aussi, à plus tard!
conversation.translation: You too, see you later!

phrases.reserving_table: Je voudrais réserver une table pour deux, s'il vous plaît
phrases.asking_menu: Pourrions-nous voir le menu, s'il vous plaît?
phrases.ordering_food: Je prendrai le saumon grillé avec des légumes
phrases.asking_bill: Pourrions-nous avoir l'addition, s'il vous plaît?

grammar.explanation: Use 'Je voudrais' (I would like) for polite requests. Add 's'il vous plaît' (please) for extra politeness.

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Bonsoir. Nous avons une réservation au nom de Johnson.
conversation.translation: Good evening. We have a reservation under Johnson.

conversation.speaker: Hôte
conversation.text: Bienvenue! Votre table est prête. Par ici, s'il vous plaît.
conversation.translation: Welcome! Your table is ready. Right this way, please.

conversation.speaker: Serveur
conversation.text: Voici vos menus. Puis-je vous apporter quelque chose à boire?
conversation.translation: Here are your menus. Can I start you with something to drink?

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Oui, nous prendrons de l'eau pour l'instant. Nous avons besoin de quelques minutes pour décider.
conversation.translation: Yes, we'll both have water for now. We need a few minutes to decide on food.

phrases.booking_hotel: J'ai une réservation au nom de Smith
phrases.at_airport: Quelle porte pour le vol vers Paris?
phrases.transportation: Combien coûte un billet pour le centre-ville?
phrases.emergency: J'ai besoin d'aide, j'ai perdu mon passeport

grammar.explanation: Start with 'Excusez-moi' (Excuse me) and use 'Où est' (Where is) for locations.

conversation.speaker: Touriste
conversation.text: Excusez-moi, pourriez-vous m'aider? Je cherche le musée du Louvre.
conversation.translation: Excuse me, could you help me? I'm looking for the Louvre Museum.

conversation.speaker: Local
conversation.text: Bien sûr! C'est à environ 15 minutes d'ici. Allez tout droit, puis tournez à gauche à la banque.
conversation.translation: Of course! It's about 15 minutes from here. Go straight, then turn left at the bank.

conversation.speaker: Touriste
conversation.text: Merci beaucoup! Dois-je marcher ou prendre le métro?
conversation.translation: Thank you so much! Should I walk or take the metro?

conversation.speaker: Local
conversation.text: Marcher est agréable, c'est une belle journée. Vous verrez beaucoup de magasins en chemin.
conversation.translation: Walking is nice, it's a beautiful day. You'll see many shops along the way.

phrases.asking_phone: Quel est votre numéro de téléphone?
phrases.counting_items: J'ai besoin de trois pommes et deux bananes

grammar.explanation: French numbers have specific patterns. Learn 1-10 first, then 11-20 have unique forms.

conversation.speaker: Commerçant
conversation.text: Cela fera quinze euros, s'il vous plaît.
conversation.translation: That will be fifteen euros, please.

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Voici vingt euros.
conversation.translation: Here is twenty euros.

conversation.speaker: Commerçant
conversation.text: Merci. Votre monnaie est cinq euros.
conversation.translation: Thank you. Your change is five euros.

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Parfait. Bonne journée!
conversation.translation: Perfect. Have a nice day!

phrases.introducing_family: Voici ma mère, elle s'appelle Maria
phrases.asking_about_family: Combien de frères et sœurs as-tu?
phrases.describing_family: J'ai deux frères et une sœur
phrases.family_activities: Nous aimons dîner ensemble tous les dimanches
phrases.family_events: Nous visitons mes cousins ce week-end

grammar.explanation: Use 'mon/ma/mes' for 'my' depending on gender and number: mon père (my father), ma mère (my mother), mes parents (my parents).

conversation.speaker: Maria
conversation.text: Voici une photo de ma famille. Ce sont mes parents.
conversation.translation: This is a photo of my family. These are my parents.

conversation.speaker: Jean
conversation.text: Ils ont l'air charmants! Combien de frères et sœurs as-tu?
conversation.translation: They look lovely! How many siblings do you have?

conversation.speaker: Maria
conversation.text: J'ai un grand frère et une petite sœur. Mon frère vit à Londres.
conversation.translation: I have one older brother and one younger sister. My brother lives in London.

conversation.speaker: Jean
conversation.text: C'est sympa. Tu lui rends souvent visite?
conversation.translation: That's nice. Do you visit him often?

phrases.asking_size: Avez-vous ceci dans une taille plus grande?
phrases.making_payment: Je voudrais payer par carte de crédit, s'il vous plaît
phrases.returning_item: Je voudrais échanger ceci, ça ne me va pas

grammar.explanation: Use 'Je cherche' (I'm looking for) and 'Avez-vous' (Do you have) when shopping.

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Excusez-moi, je cherche ce pull en taille moyenne.
conversation.translation: Excuse me, I'm looking for this sweater in a medium size.

conversation.speaker: Vendeur
conversation.text: Je vais vérifier notre stock. Oui, nous avons la taille moyenne. Voulez-vous l'essayer?
conversation.translation: Let me check our stock. Yes, we have medium. Would you like to try it on?

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Oui, s'il vous plaît. Où sont les cabines d'essayage?
conversation.translation: Yes, please. Where are the fitting rooms?

conversation.speaker: Vendeur
conversation.text: Juste au coin à gauche. Faites-moi savoir si vous avez besoin d'une autre taille.
conversation.translation: Just around the corner to your left. Let me know if you need a different size.

phrases.weather_preference: Je préfère les jours ensoleillés aux jours pluvieux

grammar.explanation: Use 'il fait' for weather conditions: il fait beau (it's nice), il fait froid (it's cold).
examples: Il fera froid (it will be cold)

conversation.speaker: Personne A
conversation.text: Belle journée aujourd'hui, n'est-ce pas?
conversation.translation: Beautiful day today, isn't it?

conversation.speaker: Personne B
conversation.text: Oui, le soleil est magnifique. Bien mieux que la pluie d'hier.
conversation.translation: Yes, the sun is wonderful. Much better than yesterday's rain.

conversation.speaker: Personne A
conversation.text: J'ai entendu qu'il pourrait pleuvoir encore demain.
conversation.translation: I heard it might rain again tomorrow though.

conversation.speaker: Personne B
conversation.text: Vraiment? Je devrais prendre mon parapluie alors.
conversation.translation: Really? I should take my umbrella then.

phrases.morning_routine: Je me réveille à sept heures
phrases.work_schedule: Je commence à travailler à neuf heures du matin
phrases.evening_activities: Après le travail, je vais à la salle de sport
phrases.weekend_routine: Le week-end, je dors jusqu'à neuf heures
phrases.daily_habits: Je lis généralement avant de m'endormir

grammar.explanation: Use reflexive verbs for daily routines: je me lève (I wake up), je me douche (I shower).

conversation.speaker: Marie
conversation.text: À quelle heure te réveilles-tu habituellement?
conversation.translation: What time do you usually wake up?

conversation.speaker: Jean
conversation.text: Je me réveille à six heures et demie pendant la semaine. Et toi?
conversation.translation: I wake up at six-thirty during the week. What about you?

conversation.speaker: Marie
conversation.text: Je ne suis pas du matin. Je me réveille à sept heures et demie.
conversation.translation: I'm not a morning person. I wake up at seven-thirty.

conversation.speaker: Jean
conversation.text: Tu as de la chance! Je dois prendre le train tôt pour aller au travail.
conversation.translation: Lucky you! I have to catch the early train to work.

grammar.explanation: Spanish sentences typically follow Subject-Verb-Object order. Questions are formed by inversion or adding question marks.

conversation.speaker: Turista
conversation.text: Disculpe, ¿dónde está la estación de tren?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, where is the train station?

conversation.speaker: Local
conversation.text: Está recto, como a cinco minutos caminando.
conversation.translation: It's straight ahead, about five minutes walk.

conversation.speaker: Turista
conversation.text: ¡Muchas gracias!
conversation.translation: Thank you very much!

conversation.speaker: Local
conversation.text: De nada. ¡Que tenga un buen día!
conversation.translation: You're welcome. Have a good day!

phrases.describing_color: Mi color favorito es el azul
phrases.color_preferences: Me gustan más los colores oscuros que los claros
phrases.color_combinations: El rojo y el blanco se ven bien juntos
phrases.nature_colors: El cielo está muy azul hoy

grammar.explanation: Spanish adjectives must agree in gender and number with the nouns they modify.

conversation.speaker: Cliente
conversation.text: Estoy buscando un abrigo nuevo.
conversation.translation: I'm looking for a new coat.

conversation.speaker: Dependiente
conversation.text: ¿De qué color está interesado? Tenemos negro, azul marino y marrón.
conversation.translation: What color are you interested in? We have black, navy, and brown.

conversation.speaker: Cliente
conversation.text: Creo que prefiero el azul marino. ¿Podría probármelo?
conversation.translation: I think I prefer the navy blue one. Could I try it on?

conversation.speaker: Dependiente
conversation.text: ¡Por supuesto! Los probadores están por allí.
conversation.translation: Of course! The fitting rooms are over there.

phrases.reserving_table: Quisiera reservar una mesa para dos, por favor
phrases.asking_menu: ¿Nos puede traer el menú, por favor?
phrases.ordering: Voy a pedir el pollo asado
phrases.dietary: Soy alérgico a los frutos secos

grammar.explanation: Use conditional/polite forms like 'Quisiera' or 'Me gustaría' to be polite when ordering.

conversation.speaker: Cliente
conversation.text: Buenas tardes, ¿tienen mesa disponible?
conversation.translation: Good afternoon, do you have a table available?

conversation.speaker: Host
conversation.text: Sí, por aquí, por favor.
conversation.translation: Yes, this way, please.

conversation.speaker: Camarero
conversation.text: ¿Qué van a tomar?
conversation.translation: What will you have?

conversation.speaker: Cliente
conversation.text: Para empezar, una ensalada y luego el pescado, gracias.
conversation.translation: To start, a salad and then the fish, thank you.

phrases.asking_schedule: ¿A qué hora sale el próximo tren?
phrases.buying_ticket: Quisiera dos billetes a Madrid, por favor
phrases.taking_taxi: ¿Cuánto cuesta un taxi hasta el centro?

grammar.explanation: Use verbs like 'salir' (to depart) and time expressions (a las 8:00) when talking about transport.
examples: El tren sale a las nueve.

conversation.speaker: Turista
conversation.text: Disculpe, ¿dónde está la estación de tren?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, where is the train station?

conversation.speaker: Local
conversation.text: A dos calles, gire a la derecha y la verá.
conversation.translation: Two blocks away, turn right and you'll see it.

conversation.speaker: Turista
conversation.text: ¿Cuánto tarda el tren hasta Barcelona?
conversation.translation: How long does the train take to Barcelona?

conversation.speaker: Local
conversation.text: Aproximadamente tres horas.
conversation.translation: Approximately three hours.

phrases.talking_hobbies: Me gusta leer en mi tiempo libre
phrases.inviting: ¿Quieres venir a jugar al fútbol este fin de semana?
phrases.describing_skills: Toco la guitarra desde hace cinco años
phrases.suggesting_activity: Podemos ir a una exposición de arte

grammar.explanation: Use 'gustar' to express likes: Me gusta(n) + noun or infinitive verb.
examples: No me gustan los deportes de invierno.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?
conversation.translation: What do you do in your free time?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Me gusta pintar y caminar en el parque.
conversation.translation: I like to paint and walk in the park.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: ¿Te gustaría unirte al club de lectura?
conversation.translation: Would you like to join the book club?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Sí, suena muy bien.
conversation.translation: Yes, sounds great.

phrases.formal_greeting: Guten Tag, wie geht es Ihnen?
phrases.evening_greeting: Guten Abend, wie war Ihr Tag?
phrases.polite_response: Mir geht es gut, danke der Nachfrage

grammar.explanation: In German, use 'Sie' for formal situations and 'du' for informal ones. Verbs conjugate differently.

conversation.speaker: Alex
conversation.text: Guten Morgen, Sarah! Wie geht es dir?
conversation.translation: Good morning, Sarah! How are you?

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.text: Guten Morgen, Alex! Mir geht es gut, danke. Und dir?
conversation.translation: Good morning, Alex! I'm doing well, thank you. How about you?

conversation.speaker: Alex
conversation.text: Mir geht es sehr gut, danke! Einen schönen Tag noch!
conversation.translation: I'm great, thanks! Have a good day!

conversation.speaker: Sarah
conversation.text: Dir auch, bis später!
conversation.translation: You too, see you later!

phrases.formal_greeting: Good morning, how do you do?
phrases.introducing_yourself: Hi, I'm [Name]. Nice to meet you.
phrases.evening_greeting: Good evening, how was your day?

grammar.explanation: Use different greetings depending on formality: 'Good morning' (formal) vs 'Hi' (informal).
examples: How are you? / How're you doing?

conversation.speaker: Sam
conversation.text: Good morning! How are you?
conversation.translation: Good morning! How are you?

conversation.speaker: Rae
conversation.text: I'm good, thanks! And you?
conversation.translation: I'm good, thanks! And you?

conversation.speaker: Sam
conversation.text: Doing well, thanks. Have a great day!
conversation.translation: Doing well, thanks. Have a great day!

conversation.speaker: Rae
conversation.text: You too!
conversation.translation: You too!

grammar.explanation: Use who/what/where/when/why/how to form basic questions in English.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Excuse me, where is the nearest bus stop?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, where is the nearest bus stop?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Two blocks down, on the left.
conversation.translation: Two blocks down, on the left.

grammar.explanation: Use 'Lei' for formal address and 'tu' for informal. Verb endings change accordingly.

conversation.speaker: Luca
conversation.text: Ciao Sara! Come va?
conversation.translation: Hi Sara! How are you?

conversation.speaker: Sara
conversation.text: Bene, grazie! E tu?
conversation.translation: Good, thanks! And you?

phrases.booking_hotel: Ho una prenotazione a nome di [Name]
phrases.at_airport: Qual è il gate per Roma?
phrases.transportation: Quanto costa un taxi fino al centro?

grammar.explanation: Use 'vorrei' or 'posso' when making polite requests or asking permission.

conversation.speaker: Tourist
conversation.text: Scusi, come arrivo al Colosseo?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, how do I get to the Colosseum?

conversation.speaker: Local
conversation.text: Prenda la metro linea B e scenda a Colosseo.
conversation.translation: Take metro line B and get off at Colosseo.

grammar.explanation: Modern Standard Arabic is used in formal settings; many dialects are used in conversation. Pronouns and verb forms differ by dialect.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: مرحبا، كيف حالك؟
conversation.translation: Hello, how are you?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: أنا بخير، شكرا. وأنت؟
conversation.translation: I'm fine, thank you. And you?

grammar.explanation: Arabic typically uses Verb-Subject-Object or Subject-Verb-Object; pronouns attach to verbs and nouns.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: أين أقرب محطة حافلات؟
conversation.translation: Where is the nearest bus station?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: امشِ إلى الأمام ثم انعطف يمينًا.
conversation.translation: Walk straight then turn right.

vocabulary.translation: ありがとうございます

phrases.formal_greeting: はじめまして、よろしくお願いします
phrases.polite_response: 元気です、ありがとうございます

grammar.explanation: Japanese has different politeness levels (casual, polite, honorific). Use ます/です for polite speech.
examples: 行く -> 行きます (informal -> polite)
ありがとう -> ありがとうございます (casual -> polite)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: こんにちは、元気ですか？
conversation.translation: Hello, how are you?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: はい、元気です。ありがとう。
conversation.translation: Yes, I'm fine. Thank you.

grammar.explanation: Particles (は/が/を) mark topic/subject/object. Verb comes at the end of the sentence.
examples: 私は学生です (I am a student)
駅に行きます (I go to the station)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: すみません、切符はいくらですか？
conversation.translation: Excuse me, how much is the ticket?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: 500円です。
conversation.translation: It's 500 yen.

grammar.explanation: Chinese uses Subject-Verb-Object order. Measure words are required with nouns.
examples: 他去学校 (He goes to school)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: 你好，请问车站在哪里？
conversation.translation: Hello, where is the station?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: 往前走，右转就到了。
conversation.translation: Go forward and turn right.

grammar.explanation: Use number + measure word + noun for counting (e.g., 三个苹果).

conversation.speaker: Seller
conversation.text: 这个多少钱？
conversation.translation: How much is this?

conversation.speaker: Buyer
conversation.text: 二十块。
conversation.translation: 20 yuan.

grammar.explanation: Use 'você' in Brazil for neutral/formal, 'tu' in some regions for informal. Verb conjugations differ.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Bom dia! Onde fica a estação?
conversation.translation: Good morning! Where is the station?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Vá em frente e vire à esquerda.
conversation.translation: Go straight and turn left.

phrases.reserving_table: Gostaria de reservar uma mesa para dois, por favor
phrases.asking_menu: Podemos ver o cardápio, por favor?

grammar.explanation: Use 'Gostaria de' or 'Queria' for polite requests.
examples: Gostaria de um café, por favor.

conversation.speaker: Cliente
conversation.text: Temos reserva no nome Silva.
conversation.translation: We have a reservation under Silva.

conversation.speaker: Host
conversation.text: Claro, esta é sua mesa.
conversation.translation: Sure, this is your table.

grammar.explanation: Russian uses cases for nouns; greetings vary by formality (Вы vs ты).

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Здравствуйте! Как вы сегодня?
conversation.translation: Hello! How are you today?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Хорошо, спасибо. А вы?
conversation.translation: Good, thank you. And you?

grammar.explanation: Russian nouns change with cases; word order is flexible but cases show roles.
examples: Я иду в магазин (I am going to the shop)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Извините, где метро?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, where is the metro?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Идите прямо, затем налево.
conversation.translation: Go straight, then left.

grammar.explanation: Korean uses honorifics and polite verb endings like -요 and -습니다 depending on formality.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: 안녕하세요! 오늘 어때요?
conversation.translation: Hello! How are you today?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: 잘 지내고 있어요, 감사합니다.
conversation.translation: I'm doing well, thank you.

grammar.explanation: Particles like 은/는/이/가 mark topic and subject; verbs at end indicate tense and politeness.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: 실례합니다, 여기 버스 정류장이 어디인가요?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, where is the bus stop?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: 저기 오른쪽에 있어요.
conversation.translation: It's over there on the right.

phrases.introducing_yourself: मेरा नाम [Name] है, मिलकर खुशी हुई

grammar.explanation: Hindi uses postpositions and verb agreement with gender and number.
examples: मैं जा रहा हूँ (I am going)
वह मेरी दोस्त है (She is my friend)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: नमस्ते, आप कैसे हैं?
conversation.translation: Hello, how are you?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद!
conversation.translation: I'm fine, thank you!

phrases.asking_help: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?

grammar.explanation: Hindi uses postpositions (e.g., में, पर) and verbs agree with the subject in gender and number.
examples: मैं घर जा रहा हूँ (I am going home)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: मुझे टिकट कितने का मिलेगा?
conversation.translation: How much will the ticket cost?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: यह दो सौ रुपये है।
conversation.translation: It is 200 rupees.

grammar.explanation: Turkish uses suffixes for grammatical functions and vowel harmony rules for suffix forms.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Merhaba! Bugün nasılsın?
conversation.translation: Hello! How are you today?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: İyiyim, teşekkürler.
conversation.translation: I'm fine, thanks.

grammar.explanation: Turkish uses suffixes for cases and verb conjugation; word order is generally SOV.

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Affedersiniz, durak nerede?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, where is the stop?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: İleri doğru yürü, sonra sağa dön.
conversation.translation: Walk forward, then turn right.

phrases.formal_greeting: Goedemorgen, hoe gaat het met u?
phrases.introducing_yourself: Ik heet [Name], leuk je te ontmoeten

grammar.explanation: Dutch uses V2 word order for main clauses and different pronouns for formality (u vs jij).

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Hallo, weet u waar het station is?
conversation.translation: Hello, do you know where the station is?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Ja, ga rechtdoor en sla links af.
conversation.translation: Yes, go straight and turn left.

grammar.explanation: Dutch articles de/het and adjective endings must be learned; V2 word order applies.
examples: Ik wil dit kopen (I want to buy this)
Heeft u dit in maat M? (Do you have this in size M?)

conversation.speaker: Klant
conversation.text: Is dit in een kleinere maat?
conversation.translation: Is this available in a smaller size?

conversation.speaker: Verkoper
conversation.text: Ik zal voor je kijken.
conversation.translation: I'll check for you.

grammar.explanation: Swedish uses definite suffixes on nouns and V2 word order for main clauses.
examples: Jag är student (I am a student)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Hej! Var ligger närmaste tunnelbana?
conversation.translation: Hi! Where is the nearest subway?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Gå rakt fram och ta första höger.
conversation.translation: Go straight and take the first right.

phrases.buying_ticket: Jag skulle vilja köpa en biljett
phrases.inquiring_transportation: Hur mycket kostar en taxi till centrum?

grammar.explanation: Swedish verbs do not conjugate for person; V2 word order is used in main clauses.
examples: Jag åker tåg (I take the train)
När går bussen? (When does the bus leave?)

conversation.speaker: A
conversation.text: Ursäkta, hur kommer jag till flygplatsen?
conversation.translation: Excuse me, how do I get to the airport?

conversation.speaker: B
conversation.text: Ta bussen nummer 5 från stationen.
conversation.translation: Take bus number 5 from the station.
